notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This subject is mentioned briefly or beside others, so the draft is short and states only what the cited ayat state. The chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God made the house a place of return and of safety for people, and a place where Ibrahim stood is to be taken as a place of prayer.
God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail: they were to purify His house for those who go around it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate.
Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail is named in the same verse beside him.
A prayer follows in the first person plural, asking the Lord to accept from the speakers, and calling Him the One who hears and knows.

The prayer goes on to ask that both speakers be made submissive to Him, that a community submissive to Him come from their offspring, that He show them their rites of worship, and that He turn to them; it calls Him the One who accepts repentance, the Merciful.
In a prayer, Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this land secure and to keep him and his sons away from worshipping idols.
Later in the same prayer, the speaker praises God, who gave him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age, and says that his Lord hears prayer.

chapters.summary_md: God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail to purify His house for those who go around it, stay in it and pray [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, with Ismail named beside him, and a prayer follows [c3][c4]. In another prayer, the speaker praises God for giving him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age [c7].
chapters.body_md:
God made the house a place of return and of safety for people [c1]. A place where Ibrahim stood is to be taken as a place of prayer [c1].

God made a covenant with Ibrahim and Ismail: they were to purify His house for those who go around it, those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house, and Ismail is named in the same verse beside him [c3]. A prayer follows in the first person plural, asking the Lord to accept from the speakers [c4]. It goes on to ask that both speakers be made submissive to Him, that a community submissive to Him come from their offspring, that He show them their rites of worship, and that He turn to them [c5].

In another prayer, Ibrahim asked his Lord to make this land secure and to keep him and his sons away from worshipping idols [c6]. Later in the same prayer, the speaker praises God, who gave him Ismail and Ishaq in his old age, and says that his Lord hears prayer [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The covenant names both men as the ones charged with purifying the house, and names the people the house is for: those who go around it, those who stay, those who bow and prostrate [c2]. The verse on the foundations names Ibrahim as the one who raises them and Ismail beside him [c3]. The prayer that follows speaks of 'us' and, in the next verse, of both speakers together [c4][c5]. The verse that names Ismail and Ishaq as a gift does not name its speaker; it sits inside the prayer that Ibrahim begins, and the gift is given in old age [c6][c7].
chapters.kids_md: God asked Ibrahim and Ismail to keep His house pure for the people who come to go around it and to pray [c2]. Ibrahim raised the foundations of the house and Ismail was named beside him [c3]. A prayer followed, asking God to accept their work [c4]. In another prayer, the speaker thanked God for giving him Ismail and Ishaq when he was old [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the covenant shows a task shared by a pair, since both are named in it [c2]. Another is that the work is followed by a prayer for acceptance, so that building is joined to turning to God [c4][c5]. A further reading is that thanks for a gift can sit in the same prayer as a request to be kept from idol worship [c6][c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the verses do not name the place where the house stood, its size, how long the work took, or how old Ismail was.
- Not established: who speaks the prayer after the foundations. The text gives a plural 'us' and a form for both speakers, and does not name them.
- Not established: whether Ismail took part in the raising of the foundations or is named beside Ibrahim for another reason; the wording names him right after Ibrahim and says no more.
- Not established: what 'purify' covers in the covenant.
- Not established: the age of Ibrahim, Ismail or Ishaq, or how far apart the sons were born.
- Not established: which land the other prayer means by 'this land'. The verses of that prayer between the ones used here are not told in this chapter.

claims.statement_en: Ismail is named for remembrance and is described as true to his promise, and as a messenger and a prophet.
He used to tell his household to pray and to give zakat, and he was one with whom his Lord was pleased.

chapters.summary_md: Ismail is described as true to his promise, a messenger and a prophet [c1]. He told his household to pray and give zakat, and his Lord was pleased with him [c2].
chapters.body_md: Ismail is named for remembrance and is described as true to his promise, and as a messenger and a prophet [c1]. He used to tell his household to pray and to give zakat, and he was one with whom his Lord was pleased [c2].
chapters.deep_md: Ismail is described as true to his promise, as a messenger and as a prophet [c1]. The verse after it adds his instruction to his household and his Lord's pleasure with him [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Ismail kept his promises [c1]. He told his family to pray and to give zakat, and God was pleased with him [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the verses place keeping a promise beside caring for one's own household in prayer [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which promise is meant, or to whom it was made.
- Not established: whether the Arabic word for his household means his family or his people; this draft keeps 'household'.
- Not established: where Ismail lived, to whom he was sent, or what his message was.

chapters.title_en: Among the patient and the best

claims.statement_en: Ismail is named together with Idris and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the patient.
God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous.
Ismail is named again, with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best.

chapters.summary_md: Ismail is named with Idris and Dhul-Kifl as one of the patient [c1]. God admitted them into His mercy and called them righteous [c2]. In another passage Ismail is named with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl as one of the best [c3].
chapters.body_md:
Ismail is named together with Idris and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the patient [c1]. God says that He admitted them into His mercy, and that they were among the righteous [c2].

Ismail is named again, with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl, and each of them is described as one of the best [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The passages group Ismail with different companions: Idris and Dhul-Kifl in one [c1], Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl in the other [c3]. The passage with Idris adds that God admitted them to His mercy and that they were righteous [c2].
chapters.kids_md: God named Ismail with Idris and Dhul-Kifl and said each of them was patient [c1]. God took them into His mercy [c2]. In another place God named Ismail with Alyasa and Dhul-Kifl and said each was among the best [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that patience is the quality singled out in the passage with Idris and that mercy is joined to it [c1][c2]. The passage with Alyasa names a different quality, being among the best [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: what Ismail was patient in, or when or where.
- Not established: the sense in which the passage with Alyasa calls them 'the best'; the verse gives the word and no example.
- Not established: whether the lists describe one gathering or separate ones.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, about this prophet. None is used in this draft.

The inventory does not include the passage on the vision of a sacrifice (37:99-113), and this draft does not use it. That passage does not name the son, and this draft does not decide who he is; a scholar should say how the page should treat the question.
2:127-128: the prayer has no verb of speech and no named speaker; the draft states only the plural wording and the dual 'both', and leaves the speakers open. A scholar should check the wording.
2:127: the draft says Ismail is named beside Ibrahim and does not say that he raised the foundations; a scholar should decide whether the Arabic supports saying more.
14:39: the speaker is not named in that verse; the draft reads it as Ibrahim because it sits in the prayer opened by his name. The verses 14:36-38 and 14:40-41 are not used.
19:55: the Arabic word that can mean household or people is rendered 'household'.
The prayers at 2:126 and 2:129 and the rest of 14:35-41 are Ibrahim's prayers that do not name Ismail and are not used.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later writers gave Ismail a place of residence, a mother, a lifespan and a role in the house; none of this is used.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
